verdicts.title: A Ballistic Monte Carlo Approximation of π
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We compute a Monte Carlo approximation of π using importance sampling with shots coming out of a Mossberg 500 pump-action shotgun as the proposal distribution. An approximated value of 3.131 is obtained, corresponding to a 0.33% error on the exact value of π. To our knowledge, this represents the first attempt at estimating π using such method, thus opening up new perspectives towards computing mathematical constants using everyday tools.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses a Monte Carlo approximation of π, which does not interact with the specific claim about cumulative entropy and balanced separator size in resolution proof complexity.

verdicts.title: An improved analytic Method for calculating $π(x)$
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We present an improved version of the analytic method for calculating $π(x)$, the number of prime numbers not exceeding $x$. We implemented this method in cooperation with J. Franke, T. Kleinjung and A. Jost and calculated the value $π(10^{25})$.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The cited paper's abstract is about calculating the number of prime numbers not exceeding a given value, which is unrelated to the conjecture regarding the cumulative-entropy analogue of space lower bounds in resolution proof complexity.
